...vim-repro/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/ai.lua:1611: in function 'find_best_match' ...vim-repro/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/ai.lua:1417: in function 'find_next' ...vim-repro/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/ai.lua:1439: in function 'find_textobject_region' ...vim-repro/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/ai.lua:611: in function 'find_textobject' ...vim-repro/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/ai.lua:1056: in function 'select_textobject' [string ":lua"]:1: in main chunk ``` I had a quick look at the commit and there seems to be a typo on line 1000: https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/commit/9c03eed61df7bc5426106f3e6aa2a896d84e3160#diff-4cef5e8622b16063c2d5ce8cfb4c93505308a0f629be3aa7760423dc25c98b04L997-R1002 The indices in the `to` table have been incremented. I couldn't find a reason for this, and the added comment seems to contradict it too. Reducing them back to 3 and 4 does fix this problem for me: `function(r) return { from = { line = r[1] + 1, col = r[2] + 1 }, to = { line = r[3] + 1, col = r[4] } } end,`. ### Reproduction 1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory: - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows 2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'. Populate it with the following content: ```lua -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed) vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw') local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim" local clone_cmd = { "git", "clone", "--depth=1", "https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim", mini_path } vim.fn.system(clone_cmd) vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw') -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available vim.cmd("packadd mini.nvim") require("mini.deps").setup() MiniDeps.add("nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter") MiniDeps.add("nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter-textobjects") -- Set up 'mini.ai' local ai = require("mini.ai") local spec_treesitter = ai.gen_spec.treesitter ai.setup({ custom_textobjects = { p = spec_treesitter({ a = "@parameter.outer", i = "@parameter.inner" }, { use_nvim_treesitter = true }), }, }) ``` 3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro"). Wait for all dependencies to install. 4. Open the config file we just created, for example `:e ~/.config/nvim-repro/init.lua` on Unix. 5. Select the first parameter textobject in the file by pressing `vip`. Observe that this correctly selects `'echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw'` on line 2. 6. Exit visual mode ``. 7. Now try to select the parameter using `a` instead of `i` by pressing `vap`. Observe that this errors.

comment_data.body:
Thanks, for the issue!

I can reproduce, but the mentioned diff is not a typo. The reason for using 4 and 5 is mentioned just above in the comment:

```lua
-- Return array of regions. Input ranges are 0-based, end-exclusive, with
-- `row1-col1-byte1-row2-col2-byte2` (i.e. "range six") format
```

So as index 3 is for byte offset of the left edge, the row and column for the right edge should be at indices 4 and 5. It might be somehow related to the custom [`#make-range!` directive](https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter-textobjects/blob/89ebe73cd2836db80a22d9748999ace0241917a5/queries/lua/textobjects.scm#L78) and how it is used in 'nvim-treesitter' functions to find matches.

The current state does work without errors on the `main` branch of both 'nvim-treesitter' and 'nvim-treesitter-textobjects' ( and not the default `master` branch). It is just not entirely correct specifically for this case of `@paramter.outer` and will be addressed after merging #1850.

I'll take a look, hopefully, tomorrow.

Yes, indeed. It is 'nvim-treesitter' that returns "range four" for captures that use `#make-range!` directives (maybe some others), but "range six" for normal cases. This should be pretty straightforward to account for in 'mini.ai'.

Just for possible future use, more investigation lead to the following behavior on `master` branch of 'nvim-treesitter':
- The newly used `vim.treesitter.get_range()` advertises that it [only returns "range six"](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/e6ce067f02ed07501093e79dc56466fada8652a1/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter.lua#L198) type. It has custom logic accounting for several ways to get range, but the most common one is [using `TSNode:range(true)`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/e6ce067f02ed07501093e79dc56466fada8652a1/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter.lua#L207) method, where `true` argument means "return range six". It also assumes that input `node` is actual tree-sitter node (i.e. `TSNode`).
- In turn, 'nvim-treesitter' constructs tree-sitter node [*manually*](https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter/blob/42fc28ba918343ebfd5565147a42a26580579482/lua/nvim-treesitter/query.lua#L282) when dealing with custom directives, like `#make-range!`.
- Custom TS range in turn defines own [`range()` method](https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter/blob/42fc28ba918343ebfd5565147a42a26580579482/lua/nvim-treesitter/tsrange.lua#L118-L120) which only return "range four" type of range.

I.e. in the end of the day, it is an issue in how 'nvim-treesitter' doesn't correctly mocks `TSNode` type for its own directives. Ideally, it should be resolved on 'nvim-treesitter' side and it is not hard to do (`start_pos` and `end_pos` also contain byte offset numbers). But all development on `master` branch has stopped and `main` branch doesn't contain custom directives.

So the only way to move forward is to either ignore the error or adjust on 'mini.ai' side. The latter is more practical and there is a concise way to do it.
This should now be resolved on latest `main`. Thanks again for mentioning this!
